Getting started with buckethost

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

buckethost turns any S3-compatible bucket into a browsable, remotely readable data repository. This vignette covers day-to-day use, including uploading local files. For moving a large dataset from Google Drive, and for requesting an Arbutus allocation, see vignette("migration-workflow").

Configure once

Functions resolve connection details from options (or BUCKETHOST_* environment variables). Set them once — ideally in your .Rprofile:

library(buckethost)

options(
  buckethost.endpoint  = "https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca",
  buckethost.container = "529feda02d404836b0e91b1d360b4df0:predictiveecology",
  buckethost.remote    = "arbutus"   # name of the rclone remote
)

Arbutus moved in 2026. The old endpoint, object-arbutus.cloud.computecanada.ca, is retired and the package default still points at it, so set buckethost.endpoint as above. On the new endpoint, public URLs include the project id (https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca/<project-id>:<bucket>/<key>), so the container includes it too; the rclone-based functions drop it themselves. buckethost.remote is whatever you named your rclone remote. The predictiveecology bucket allows public reads but not public listing, so bucketLs() (and with it generateIndexes() and makeMirrorManifest()) lists through your rclone remote instead, which needs write access set up.

Three identifiers, easily confused:

  • endpoint — the storage host, no bucket name.
  • container — the bucket name.
  • remote — the local name of your rclone remote (from rclone config). Only the mutating functions (bucketUpload(), bucketDelete(), bucketVerify(), and uploading indexes) use it.

bucketBaseUrl() and bucketRcloneRemote() show how these combine:

bucketBaseUrl()        #> "https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca/529feda02d404836b0e91b1d360b4df0:predictiveecology"
bucketRcloneRemote()   #> "arbutus:predictiveecology"

Discover what’s there

bucketLs() reads the bucket’s public listing API (no credentials needed for a public-read bucket) and returns one row per object. If the bucket refuses anonymous listing, it lists with your rclone remote instead:

objs <- bucketLs(prefix = "SCANFI_v2/1985")
head(objs)
#>                                          key      size                  modified
#> 1 SCANFI_v2/1985/SCANFI_age_median_1985_v2.tif 154238911 2026-01-19T...

Build URLs from keys:

bucketUrl("SCANFI_v2/1985/SCANFI_age_median_1985_v2.tif")
#> "https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca/529feda02d404836b0e91b1d360b4df0:predictiveecology/SCANFI_v2/1985/..."

Read rasters remotely

bucketRaster() wraps terra::rast("/vsicurl/<url>"). For a Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, GDAL fetches only the byte ranges it needs:

r <- bucketRaster("SCANFI_v2/1985/SCANFI_age_median_1985_v2.tif")
r                       # metadata only; nothing downloaded yet

aoi <- terra::vect(my_study_area)
sub <- terra::crop(r, terra::project(aoi, terra::crs(r)))   # a few hundred KB
terra::plot(sub)

Set up write access (once)

Reading needs nothing. Uploading, deleting and verifying need S3 credentials and an rclone remote. You must be a member of the Arbutus project that owns the bucket.

EC2 (S3-compatible) credentials. The OpenStack Application Credentials in the dashboard are not what you want — those use Swift-native auth, not S3. The Horizon dashboard removed the direct “EC2 Credentials” button, so use the CLI:

pipx install python-openstackclient        # or pip install --user on Windows
source ~/Downloads/<project>-openrc.sh
openstack ec2 credentials create

This needs port 5000 (Keystone), which is blocked on many government networks. Workaround: run it once from a home network or cellular hotspot. The resulting EC2 access key + secret are portable — once created they work from anywhere over port 443. Save them to a password manager.

The arbutus rclone remote. rclone config → n (new) → name arbutus → storage s3 → provider Other → env_auth false → paste your EC2 access key / secret → region blank → endpoint https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca → location_constraint blank → acl private → Edit advanced config: yes, and set the one critical option:

force_path_style = true

Arbutus’s Swift S3 gateway doesn’t support virtual-hosted-style URLs (bucket.endpoint.com). Without force_path_style = true, every request fails with signature or DNS errors. Accept defaults for everything else. The resulting ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf should contain:

[arbutus]
type = s3
provider = Other
access_key_id = <key>
secret_access_key = <secret>
endpoint = https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca
acl = private
force_path_style = true

Test: rclone lsd arbutus: should list your container(s) with no error.

Mutate the bucket

Uploads and deletes wrap rclone and fail loudly with rclone’s own error text. rclone only transfers changes, so re-running is cheap.

bucketUpload("~/local/SCANFI/1985", "SCANFI_v2/1985",
              filterFile = "~/scanfi.filter",
              extra = c("--retries", "10", "--stats", "60s"))

res <- bucketVerify("~/local/SCANFI/1985", "SCANFI_v2/1985",
                     filterFile = "~/scanfi.filter")
res$ok

bucketDelete("SCANFI_v2/1985/obsolete.tif")          # prompts to confirm
bucketDelete("SCANFI_v2/old", recursive = TRUE,
              confirm = FALSE)                         # whole prefix, no prompt

Generate the browsable catalogue

generateIndexes() writes one index.html per folder level (sortable columns, breadcrumbs, a per-page disclaimer block) and uploads them:

generateIndexes(
  heading = "PredictiveEcology Temporary Data Repository",
  disclaimerHtml = paste0(
    "<div class='hero'><p><strong>These data are not produced by the ",
    "PredictiveEcology group</strong> and are only hosted here to ease ",
    "open data access.</p></div>"
  ),
  hostNote = "Hosted on the Digital Research Alliance of Canada's Arbutus object storage."
)

Browse the result at <endpoint>/<container>/index.html. Inspect the pages without uploading by passing dryRun = TRUE, which returns the HTML:

pages <- generateIndexes(dryRun = TRUE)
cat(pages[[""]])        # the root index.html

To customise the look, copy the shipped template and edit it:

file.copy(
  system.file("templates", "index.html", package = "buckethost"),
  "my-template.html"
)
generateIndexes(template = "my-template.html")
